name: Neon
description: Let your AI manage Neon serverless Postgres: projects, branches, compute endpoints, databases, roles, schemas, operations and consumption. It can create branches and start or suspend computes after your confirmation. Never returns passwords. With a Neon API key.
instructions:
## Neon
This connector manages **Neon** serverless Postgres through the Neon API v2 (`https://console.neon.tech/api/v2`) with an API key: organizations, projects, branches, compute endpoints (start and suspend), databases, roles, database schemas, operations and consumption. It does not run SQL (see below).

**Setup (about 2 minutes)**
1. In the Neon Console open **Account settings → API keys** (personal key: acts as you, in every organization you belong to) or **Organization settings → API keys** (organization key: only that organization's projects; a project-scoped key: only one project).
2. Create the key, copy it at once (Neon shows it only once) and paste it into `NEON_API_KEY`.
3. Install and run `neon_list_organizations`.

**Write tools need confirmation.** Before `neon_create_branch`, `neon_start_endpoint` or `neon_suspend_endpoint`, tell the user what will happen and wait for a clear yes.
- A running compute uses compute hours (CU-hours), which count against the plan's allowance or are billed on paid plans; `neon_start_endpoint` starts that meter. Computes scale to zero by themselves after the suspend timeout.
- `neon_suspend_endpoint` closes every open connection to that compute at once.
- `neon_create_branch` creates a copy-on-write branch (instant, no data copied). Branches beyond the plan's allowance and their storage changes can be billed; adding an endpoint also starts a compute. Set `expires_at` for temporary branches.
- **Switched off at install**: `neon_delete_branch` (deletes the branch and its computes; the root and default branch cannot be deleted).

**Finding things**
- `neon_list_organizations` gives the `org_id`s. With a **personal** API key, `neon_list_projects` needs `org_id` for organization projects; with an organization key it is inferred.
- `neon_list_projects` → `neon_get_project` (settings and this period's usage) → `neon_list_branches` / `neon_get_branch` (the default branch has `default: true`) → `neon_list_databases` / `neon_list_roles` / `neon_get_database_schema`. Ids: projects like `shiny-wind-028834`, branches `br-...`, computes `ep-...`.
- `neon_list_endpoints` (or `neon_get_endpoint` for one) shows each compute's state (`active`, `idle`), size range in CU and the host name.
- Every change runs as asynchronous operations: the answer lists them, and `neon_get_operation` shows when they finish (`finished`, `failed`).
- Lists page with `cursor`: pass `pagination.next` (branches) or `pagination.cursor` (projects, operations) from the previous answer.

**Usage and cost**: `neon_get_consumption` returns compute unit seconds, storage, branch counts and network transfer per project and period (hourly for the last 7 days, daily for 60 days, monthly for a year). It needs `org_id` and is available on paid plans only (Launch, Scale, Business, Enterprise). It does not wake computes. Project and branch details also show `compute_time_seconds`, `active_time_seconds`, `written_data_bytes` and `data_transfer_bytes` for the current period.

**Passwords and connection strings are never returned.** Role passwords, connection URIs and the reveal-password call are left out on purpose, so no database password reaches the AI.

**Running SQL is not part of this connector.** Neon's SQL over HTTP endpoint (`https://<endpoint host>/sql`) authenticates with a full Postgres connection string including the role's password, not with the API key, so it would put a database password in front of the AI. To query data, use the **PostgreSQL** connector with a dedicated read-only Postgres role on the Neon host (`<endpoint host>`, port 5432, SSL required). `neon_get_database_schema` still shows the tables and columns without a password.

**Common errors**
- 401 `supplied credentials do not pass authentication`: wrong or revoked API key. Neon answers 401 on every URL for a bad key.
- 403: the key may not access that project or organization (a project-scoped or organization key used elsewhere), or the plan does not include the feature (consumption history).
- 404: wrong project, branch or endpoint id. 423 `Locked`: another operation is running on the project; wait for it (`neon_list_operations`) and retry.
- 429: too many requests; wait a little and retry.

**Out of scope here**: SQL, creating or deleting projects, databases and roles, resetting role passwords, Neon Auth, the Data API, snapshots and organization administration.
prerequisites: A Neon account and an API key from the Neon Console (Account settings → API keys, or an organization's API keys). About 2 minutes.

NEON_API_KEY.label: Neon API key
NEON_API_KEY.help: Neon Console → Account settings → API keys (personal) or Organization settings → API keys. Copy it when created: Neon shows it only once.
NEON_API_KEY.patternMessage: Paste only the key as Neon shows it, without spaces and without the word Bearer.

verifyHints.401: Neon refused the API key: it is wrong or was revoked. Create a new one in the Neon Console under API keys.
verifyHints.403: The API key may not access this. A project-scoped or organization key only reaches its own project or organization.
verifyHints.rate_limited: Neon is rate limiting this key. Wait a minute and try again.

tools.name: neon_list_organizations
tools.description: List the Neon organizations the API key belongs to, with org_id, name, handle and plan. With an organization or project key it returns the one organization that owns the key. Start here for the org_id.

tools.name: neon_list_projects
tools.description: List Neon projects with id, name, region, Postgres version, organization, storage size and last compute activity. With a personal API key pass org_id for an organization's projects. Search by partial name or id.

org_id.description: Organization id (from neon_list_organizations). Needed with a personal API key for organization projects.

search.description: Filter by partial project name or id.

tools.name: neon_get_project
tools.description: Get one Neon project: region, Postgres version, default compute settings, history retention, and this billing period's compute time, active time, written data, data transfer and storage.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

tools.name: neon_list_branches
tools.description: List the branches of a Neon project with id, name, parent, state, default and protected flags, logical size and this period's compute time. Newest changes first.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

search.description: Filter by partial branch name or id.

sort_by.description: Sort field: updated_at (default), created_at or name.

tools.name: neon_get_branch
tools.description: Get one Neon branch: name, parent and branch point, state, default and protected flags, expiry, logical size and this period's compute and data usage.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

branch_id.description: Branch id, starting with 'br-', e.g. 'br-aged-salad-637688' (from neon_list_branches).

tools.name: neon_create_branch
tools.description: Create a Neon branch (an instant copy-on-write copy of a parent branch, optionally at a point in time). Confirm with the user first: extra branches and any compute you add can be billed. Pass endpoints [{"type": "read_write"}] to add a compute that starts at once. No passwords or connection strings are returned.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

name.description: Name for the new branch, e.g. 'feature-checkout'. Auto-generated if left out.

parent_id.description: Branch to copy from. Default: the project's default branch.

parent_timestamp.description: Copy the parent as it was at this time (RFC 3339, within the history retention window), e.g. '2026-10-14T08:00:00Z'.

parent_lsn.description: Copy the parent at this Postgres LSN instead of a time.

init_source.description: parent-data (default) copies schema and data; parent-schema copies only the parent's schema; schema-only creates a new root branch with the schema only.

expires_at.description: Delete the branch automatically at this time (RFC 3339), for temporary branches.

endpoints.description: Computes to create with the branch, e.g. [{"type": "read_write"}] or with sizes {"type": "read_write", "autoscaling_limit_min_cu": 0.25, "autoscaling_limit_max_cu": 1}. Leave out for a branch without compute.

tools.name: neon_delete_branch
tools.description: Delete a Neon branch and its computes, ending all their connections. Switched off at install. Confirm with the user first and name the branch; the root and default branch, and branches with children, cannot be deleted.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

branch_id.description: Branch id, starting with 'br-', e.g. 'br-aged-salad-637688' (from neon_list_branches).

tools.name: neon_list_endpoints
tools.description: List the compute endpoints of a Neon project: id, branch, read-write or read-only, state (active, idle), autoscaling range in compute units, suspend timeout, pooler and host name.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

tools.name: neon_get_endpoint
tools.description: Get one Neon compute endpoint: state, branch, type, autoscaling range, suspend timeout, last activity, start and suspend times and host name.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

endpoint_id.description: Compute endpoint id, starting with 'ep-' (from neon_list_endpoints).

tools.name: neon_start_endpoint
tools.description: Start (wake) a Neon compute endpoint. Confirm with the user first: a running compute uses billable compute hours until it scales to zero again. Follow the returned operations with neon_get_operation.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

endpoint_id.description: Compute endpoint id, starting with 'ep-' (from neon_list_endpoints).

tools.name: neon_suspend_endpoint
tools.description: Suspend a Neon compute endpoint now, which stops compute billing but closes every open connection to it. Confirm with the user first. It wakes again on the next connection.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

endpoint_id.description: Compute endpoint id, starting with 'ep-' (from neon_list_endpoints).

tools.name: neon_list_databases
tools.description: List the Postgres databases of a Neon branch with name and owner role.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

branch_id.description: Branch id, starting with 'br-', e.g. 'br-aged-salad-637688' (from neon_list_branches).

tools.name: neon_list_roles
tools.description: List the Postgres roles of a Neon branch with name, protected flag and authentication method. Passwords are never returned.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

branch_id.description: Branch id, starting with 'br-', e.g. 'br-aged-salad-637688' (from neon_list_branches).

tools.name: neon_get_database_schema
tools.description: Get the schema of one database on a Neon branch (tables, columns, types, indexes, constraints, as pg_dump-style SQL), optionally as it was at a past time. Read-only; no password needed.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

branch_id.description: Branch id, starting with 'br-', e.g. 'br-aged-salad-637688' (from neon_list_branches).

timestamp.description: Read the schema as it was at this time (RFC 3339), within the history retention window.

lsn.description: Read the schema at this Postgres LSN instead of a time.

tools.name: neon_list_operations
tools.description: List the operations of a Neon project (branch creation, compute start and suspend, config changes), newest first, with status, error and duration.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

tools.name: neon_get_operation
tools.description: Get one Neon operation: action, status (scheduling, running, finished, failed, cancelled), error, retries and duration. Use it to follow a change until it finishes.

project_id.description: Neon project id, e.g. 'shiny-wind-028834' (id from neon_list_projects).

operation_id.description: Operation id (a UUID) from an earlier answer.

tools.name: neon_get_consumption
tools.description: Get Neon consumption per project and period: compute unit seconds, root and child branch storage, instant restore storage, extra branches, snapshots and network transfer. Paid plans only; needs org_id. Does not wake computes.

granularity.description: hourly (last 168 hours), daily (last 60 days) or monthly (last year).

metrics.description: Metrics to return. Default: compute_unit_seconds, root_branch_bytes_month, child_branch_bytes_month, public_network_transfer_bytes.
